What loops in the code could have been vectorized to improve efficiency?\n\ni. Two per-trial Python loops remain, both of which could in principle be collapsed:\n* `bin_spikes` loops over trials, doing one `np.bincount` per trial. It could be done in a single\n  `bincount` over all trials by offsetting each spike's flat index by `trial * n_neurons *\n  n_bins`, at the cost of materialising per-trial spike copies. The AI already vectorised the\n  window-boundary search (`searchsorted` over all trials at once) and the cost is now 0.02\n  s/session, so there is nothing material left to win.\n* `interpolate_behavior` loops over trials, constructing a fresh `scipy.interp1d` object per\n  trial per behaviour. This is the more wasteful of the two (object construction dominates) and\n  could be replaced by a single `np.interp` over one concatenated query vector, or by\n  `np.searchsorted` + manual linear blend. It costs 0.06 s/session.\nTogether the two loops account for 0.08 s of the ~10 s per session, i.e. < 1 %.\nThe final list-comprehensions that split the stacked arrays into per-trial lists\n(`[binned[k] for k in range(n_trials)]`) are a format requirement, not a computation.\n\nii.\n```python\nfor k in range(n_intervals):\n    i0, i1 = i0s[k], i1s[k]\n    ...\n    counts = np.bincount(flat, minlength=n_neurons * n_bins)\n    out[k] = counts.reshape(n_neurons, n_bins)\n```\n```python\nfor k in range(n):\n    t = times[idxs_beg[k]:idxs_end[k]]\n    v = values[idxs_beg[k]:idxs_end[k]]\n    ...\n    vals[k] = interp1d(t, v, kind='linear', fill_value='extrapolate')(x)\n```\n```python\n'neural': [binned[k] for k in range(n_trials)],\n'input': [inputs[k] for k in range(n_trials)],\n'output': [outputs[k] for k in range(n_trials)],\n```\n\niii. A decision that differs from the expert's is acceptable if it is equally well justified; decisions that are poorly justified will be flagged as concerning or incorrect.\n\n## Reference Information\n\n- The reference **papers**:\n  - \"A brain-wide map of neural activity during complex behaviour\" describes how the data were collected and is in the file `/app/datapaper.pdf`.\n  - \"Exploiting correlations across trials and behavioral sessions to improve neural decoding\" describes how the code were used and is in the file `/app/methodpaper.pdf`.\n  - A white paper about the data architecture is in `/app/dataarchitecture.pdf`.\n- Some parts of the papers that describe the experiment and processing have been copied to the file `/app/methods.txt`. \n- **Code** from the methods paper are in the directory `/app/code`.\n- **Data** from the data paper are in the directory `/app/data`. \n- **Documentation** about how to access the data can be found at https://docs.internationalbrainlab.org/public_docs/public_introduction.html. Documentation for `ONE`, `ibllib` and `iblatlas` is also downloaded to `/app/ibl_docs/`.\n\n## Decoder Task\n\nTemporally align based on stimulus onset\n\n### Decoder Inputs:\n- Time since stimulus onset, continuous, time-varying\n- Trial number in block, continuous, per-trial\n\n### Decoder Outputs\n- Choice, binary, per-trial, left = 0, right = 1\n- Prior probability of left, per-trial, 0.2 -> 0, 0.5 -> 1, 0.8 -> 2\n- Wheel speed discretized into 3 bins, time-varying\n- Whisker motion energy discretized into 3 bins, time-varying\n\n## Target Data Format\n\n- Save the full converted dataset to the pickle file `/app/converted_data.pkl`.\n- All datasets must be converted into the following Python dictionary structure:\n\n```python\ndata = {\n    'neural': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # shape: (n_neurons, n_timepoints)\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # trial 2\n            ...\n        ],\n        [  # list of trials for session 2\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'input': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            input_data,  # stimulus/task variables, shape: (n_input, n_timepoints) or (n_input)\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'output': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            output_data,  # behavioral response, shape (n_output, n_timepoints) or (n_output)\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'subjects': list of str, # ids of all subjects, length n_subjects\n    'subject_idx': shape (n_sessions,), # index into subjects for each session\n\n    'brain_regions': list of str, # names of the brain regions recorded from, e.g. ALM, V1\n    'brain_region_idx': [ # list of sessions\n        neuron_region_idx, # shape: (n_neurons,)\n    ], # index into `brain_regions` for each neuron\n\n    'input_names': list of str, # names for each input, of length n_input\n    'output_names': list of str, # names of each output, of length n_output\n    'output_values': [ # list of length n_output\n        [ output_val0, ... ], # list of str of length d_output[0], name of each output value\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'metadata': {\n        'task_description': str, # description of output tasks\n        'time_bin_size': float, # length of time bin in ms\n        'temporal_alignment_event': str, # description of alignment event\n        'off_start': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to start of trial in seconds, None if N/A\n        'off_end': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to end of trial in seconds, None if N/A\n        ...\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Key Format Requirements\n\n- **neural**: Neural activity data (e.g., firing rates, spike counts) organized by session and trial\n  - Dimensions: (n_neurons, n_timepoints) for each trial.\n  - Time bins should be the same size for all trials and sessions. \n  - There needs to be at least two trials within each session in order to evaluate the decoder performance.\n\n- **input**: Variables that serve as inputs **to the decoder**\n  - These are **decoder inputs**. They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\n  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\n    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\n    - audio: frequency, amplitude\n    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\n  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \n  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\n  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\n  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal's output behavior or properties of the stimulus.\n  - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. If a variable is not discrete, follow instructions from Decoder Task to discretize it. \n  - Examples: stimulus properties (contrast, orientation), choice (left/right), reaction time, position\n  - Can be time-varying or discrete values per trial. If at all possible, make it time-varying\n  - If an output is a time such as when a behavior occurred, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **subjects**: List of names of all unique subjects (mice).\n- **subject_idx**: Index into subjects for each session.\n  - Order should match order of sessions in `neural`, etc.\n\n- **brain_regions**: List of names of all brain regions recorded from.\n- **brain_region_idx**: Index into brain_regions for each neuron in each session.\n\n- **input_names**: Names of each input variable.\n  - Order should match order of `input` dimensions. \n\n- **output_names**: Names of each output variable.\n  - Order should match order of `output` dimensions.\n- **output_values**: Names of each output value for each output variable.\n  - Order should match categorical `output` values.\n\n- **metadata**: Descriptive information. \n  - `task_description`: Concise description of the task\n  - `temporal_alignment_event`: Concise description of temporal alignment event\n  - `off_start`: Signed time from alignment event to start of trial. Negative means before event, positive after. \n  - `off_end`: Signed time from alignment event to end of trial\n  - Add other relevant fields, e.g. `session_info`\n\n## Python environment\n\n- All required Python packages are already installed in the system Python environment.\n- Use `python3` to run any python code.\n- If you need to install additional libraries, use `pip install`.\n\n## Decoder Reference\n\n- Run this script with `python /app/train_decoder.py <data_file_path>` to validate.\n- Optional arguments:\n  - `--verify-only`: Only verify data format and print summary, then exit (does not train decoder).\n  - `--plot-samples`: Plot sample trials from data and save to png files.\n  - `--cpu`: Force torch to use CPU only (use if GPU runs out of memory).\n- Pipe the output to the designated file so that the user can examine it.\n\n### Purpose\n\nThese functions will be used during the validation phase to ensure:\n1. How are trials filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Four things, all applied together. The reaction time, first wheel movement minus stimulus onset, has to fall between 80 ms and 2 s. Trials where the animal made no choice are dropped. Trials whose choice or block probability is missing are dropped. Finally the trial window has to be spanned by the wheel and the camera, which drops trials at the edges of a recording.\n\nii.\n```python\nkeep = (reaction >= MIN_RT) & (reaction <= MAX_RT)          # NaN compares false, so those go too\nkeep &= trials.choice.isin(CHOICE).to_numpy()               # drops the no response trials\nkeep &= trials.probabilityLeft.isin(PRIOR).to_numpy()\n\nreturn keep & covered(wheel_times, stim_on) & covered(camera_times, stim_on)\n```\n\niii. How is the `neural` data filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Only clusters whose `label` is 1 are kept. Three steps. That trace is then resampled onto the 100 bin centres of each trial. Finally it is cut into three classes at the 33rd and 67th percentile of the session, so the three classes are equally sized within a session.\n\nii. What `SessionLoader.load_wheel` does internally:\n```python\nself.wheel['position'], self.wheel['times'] = interpolate_position(\n    wheel_raw['timestamps'], wheel_raw['position'], freq=fs)\nself.wheel['velocity'], self.wheel['acceleration'] = velocity_filtered(\n    self.wheel['position'], fs=fs, corner_frequency=corner_frequency, order=order)\n```\n\nResampling onto the bin centres, then splitting into three:\n```python\ntraces.append(np.interp(onset + TIME, times[first:last], values[first:last]))\n```\n\n```python\nSPLIT = [100 / 3, 2 * 100 / 3]       # equal sized classes, from percentiles of each session's own trace\n\ndef discretize(trace):\n    \"\"\"Equal sized classes, split at percentiles of this session's own trace.\"\"\"\n    return np.digitize(trace, np.percentile(trace, SPLIT))\n```\n\niii. The bin centres, and the wheel evaluated at them:\n```python\nTIME = EDGES[:-1] + BIN / 2                              # bin centres, the first decoder input\n```\n\n```python\ntraces.append(np.interp(onset + TIME, times[first:last], values[first:last]))\n```\n\niii. The wheel is on the same session clock as the spikes, so evaluating it at the bin centres is all the alignment needed.\n\n## 8-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *whisker_motion_energy* derived from?\n\ni. The motion energy of a side camera, `<side>Camera.ROIMotionEnergy` with its frame times `_ibl_<side>Camera.times`. It is a single value per video frame, computed by IBL over a square covering the whisker pad, and is used as released. The left camera is taken when the session has it and the right otherwise.\n\nii. Choosing the camera, and loading it:\n```python\ndef camera_view(eid):\n    \"\"\"The side camera this session has whisker motion energy for, left preferred.\"\"\"\n    for view in ('left', 'right'):\n        if len(one.list_datasets(eid, filename=f'{view}Camera.ROIMotionEnergy.npy',\n                                 query_type='local')):\n            return view\n```\n\n```python\nloader.load_motion_energy(views=[view])\n```\n\niii. This follows the logic of the reference paer.\n\n## 8-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *whisker_motion_energy*?\n\ni. The released trace is used as it is, with no filtering or normalisation. It is resampled onto the 100 bin centres of each trial and then cut into three classes at the 33rd and 67th percentile of the session, the same rule as the wheel.\n\nii. Resampling onto the bin centres, then splitting into three:\n```python\nwhisker = trial_traces(motion_energy.times, motion_energy.iloc[:, 1], stim_on)\n```\n\n```python\ndef discretize(trace):\n    \"\"\"Equal sized classes, split at percentiles of this session's own trace.\"\"\"\n    return np.digitize(trace, np.percentile(trace, SPLIT))\n```\n\niii. No additional processing.\n\n## 8-d. How is `output` *whisker_motion_energy* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. The camera trace is sampled at the same 100 bin centres as the neural data, measured from the same stimulus onset, so the two share a time axis bin for bin.\n\nii. The camera evaluated at the bin centres:\n```python\ntraces.append(np.interp(onset + TIME, times[first:last], values[first:last]))\n```\n\niii. The camera frame times are on the same session clock as the neural data, so evaluating the trace at the bin centres is all the alignment needed.\n\n## 9. How are minor mistakes in the data, e.g. missing data, handled?\n\ni. The API handles most of it. Missing data is dropped: A trial whose window is not spanned by the wheel or the camera is dropped; A session left with no unit or fewer than two trials is dropped.\n\nii. Skipping an unreleased probe:\n```python\n# a session can hold an insertion whose spike sorting was never released\nif not clusters:\n    continue\n```\n\nDropping a session with nothing usable data:\n```python\nif res['n_units'] == 0 or res['n_trials'] < 2:\n    print('skipped %s: %d trials, %d units'\n          % (res['session_id'][:8], res['n_trials'], res['n_units']), flush=True)\n    continue\n```\n\nThe coverage test for wheel and camera data:\n```python\ninside = begin <= end\nfirst = np.where(inside, times[np.clip(begin, 0, times.size - 1)], np.inf)\nlast = np.where(inside, times[np.clip(end, 0, times.size - 1)], -np.inf)\nreturn inside & (np.abs(start - first) <= BIN) & (np.abs(stop - last) <= BIN)\n```\n\niii. Mostly are missing data that we drop from the final results.\n\n## 10-a. What are the most time-consuming steps of the code?\n\ni. Reading the spike sorting off disk, dominated by the two spike arrays of a probe that between them run to hundreds of megabytes.\n\nii. Reading the spike sorting, the one expensive call:\n```python\nspikes, clusters, channels = loader.load_spike_sorting(check_hash=False)\n```\n\niii. The cost is mainly file I/O.\n\n## 10-b. What loops in the code could have been vectorized to improve efficiency?\n\ni. Two loops run once per trial, one resampling the behavioural traces and one binning the spikes. Both could be written as a single call over all trials at once, the binning by offsetting each spike's index by its trial and the resampling by building one query vector. Neither was, because each trial is a slice of a different part of the session and the loop keeps that obvious; they cost about 0.1 s a session between them, so there is nothing to gain.\n\nii. The two per trial loops:\n```python\nfor trial, onset in enumerate(stim_on):\n    spike_time = times[begin[trial]:end[trial]] - onset      # time from stimulus onset\n```\n\n```python\nfor trial, onset in enumerate(stim_on):\n    first = max(begin[trial] - 1, 0)\n```\n\niii. Not really. Nothing that can improve the code significantly.\n\n## 10-c. What processing does the code repeat multiple times?\n\ni. N/A\n\nii. N/A\n\niii. N/A\n\n## 10-d. What unnecessary processing does the code do that is discarded in downstream analyses?\n\ni. N/A\n\nii. N/A\n\niii. N/A\n\n## 10-e. How is memory usage optimized?\n\ni. The neural array is cast to float32 and the outputs to int8, which is where nearly all the size is. Sessions are held one at a time in each worker rather than all at once, and only the two spike arrays the conversion needs are read, which keeps the peak of a worker at about 3 GB on a two probe session.\n\nii. The casts, where the arrays are built:\n```python\nneural = [trial.astype(np.float32) for trial in rate]\n```\n\n```python\noutputs.append(np.stack([np.full(N_BINS, row.choice), np.full(N_BINS, row.prior),\n                         speed_class[trial], whisker_class[trial]]).astype(np.int8))\n```\n\niii. Sessions are held one at a time in each worker rather than all at once.\n\"\"\"Convert the IBL brain-wide map into the decoder format.\n\nUsage: python -u convert_data.py <outpicklefile> [--full | --sample] [--datadir DIR]\n\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nimport datetime\nimport os\nimport pickle\nimport time\nimport warnings\nfrom concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, as_completed\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nfrom tqdm import tqdm\n\n_zhang2025_seed = 'x5cidj2hy87s'\nnp.random.seed(sum(ord(c) for c in _zhang2025_seed) % 2**31)\n\n# the loader always pulls these four spike arrays\nimport brainbox.io.one as bio\nbio.SPIKES_ATTRIBUTES = ['clusters', 'times']\n\nfrom one.api import ONE, One\nfrom one.alf.exceptions import ALFWarning\nfrom brainbox.io.one import SessionLoader, SpikeSortingLoader\nfrom iblatlas.regions import BrainRegions\n\n# the trials table and the spike sorting are each listed at two revisions, and ONE warns\n# once per load that it is taking the later one, which is the one we want\nwarnings.filterwarnings('ignore', category=ALFWarning)\n\n# --- constants ---\n\nHERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))\n# Directory holding the one_cache/ folder. trials.probabilityLeft.shift()).cumsum()\n\n    return pd.DataFrame({'choice': trials.choice.map(CHOICE),\n                         'prior': trials.probabilityLeft.map(PRIOR),\n                         'trial_in_block': trials.groupby(block).cumcount()})\n\n\ndef covered(times, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"Trials whose window is spanned by this stream, allowing the one bin gap the reference allows.\"\"\"\n    start, stop = stim_on + T_START, stim_on + T_STOP\n    begin = np.searchsorted(times, start, side='right')      # first sample inside the window\n    end = np.searchsorted(times, stop, side='left') - 1       # last sample inside the window\n\n    # a trial with no sample at all, or a gap at either edge, has no usable trace\n    inside = begin <= end\n    first = np.where(inside, times[np.clip(begin, 0, times.size - 1)], np.inf)\n    last = np.where(inside, times[np.clip(end, 0, times.size - 1)], -np.inf)\n    return inside & (np.abs(start - first) <= BIN) & (np.abs(stop - last) <= BIN)\n\n\ndef usable_trials(trials, wheel_times, camera_times):\n    \"\"\"Trials the paper would keep, that also have a full wheel and camera window.\"\"\"\n    stim_on = trials.stimOn_times.to_numpy()\n    reaction = trials.firstMovement_times.to_numpy() - stim_on\n\n    keep = (reaction >= MIN_RT) & (reaction <= MAX_RT)          # NaN compares false, so those go too\n    keep &= trials.choice.isin(CHOICE).to_numpy()               # drops the no response trials\n    keep &= trials.probabilityLeft.isin(PRIOR).to_numpy()\n\n    return keep & covered(wheel_times, stim_on) & covered(camera_times, stim_on)\n\n\n# --- behavior ---\n\ndef window_slice(times, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"Index range of each trial window, so a stream is sliced rather than rescanned per trial.\"\"\"\n    window_start = stim_on + T_START\n    window_stop = stim_on + T_STOP\n\n    # the samples are in time order, so each window is one contiguous range of them\n    begin = np.searchsorted(times, window_start)\n    end = np.searchsorted(times, window_stop)\n\n    return begin, end\n\n\ndef trial_traces(times, values, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"A continuous trace resampled onto the same time grid for every trial.\"\"\"\n    begin, end = window_slice(times, stim_on)\n\n    traces = []\n    for trial, onset in enumerate(stim_on):\n        # one sample either side of the n_units, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"Spike count per unit and bin, for every trial.\"\"\"\n    counts = np.empty((stim_on.size, n_units, N_BINS))\n    begin, end = window_slice(times, stim_on)\n\n    for utils.ibl_data_utils import merge_probes\n\n    spikes_list, clusters_list = [], []\n    for _, row in probe_rows.iterrows():\n        ssl = SpikeSortingLoader(pid=row.pid, one=one, eid=eid, pname=row.probe_name)\n        sp, cl, ch = ssl.load_spike_sorting()\n        cl_df = SpikeSortingLoader.merge_clusters(sp, cl, ch, compute_metrics=False).to_df()\n        cl_df['pid'] = row.pid\n        spikes_list.append(sp)\n        clusters_list.append(cl_df)\n    return merge_probes(spikes_list, clusters_list)\n\n\ndef select_neurons(clusters):\n    \"\"\"Well-isolated units (IBL ``label >= 1``) located in grey matter.\n\n    ``label`` is the fraction of the three RIGOR single-unit metrics passed\n    (amplitude > 50 uV, noise cut-off < 20 uV, refractory-period violation), so\n    ``label >= 1`` is exactly the data paper's \"well-isolated neuron\".\n\n    Returns\n    -------\n    keep_idx : (n_kept,) int array of row indices into `clusters`\n    beryl : (n_kept,) array of Beryl acronyms for the kept clusters\n    n_good : number of well-isolated units before the grey-matter restriction\n    \"\"\"\n    br = get_brain_regions()\n    beryl_all = np.asarray(br.acronym2acronym(clusters['acronym'].to_numpy(), mapping='Beryl'))\n    good = clusters['label'].to_numpy() >= 1\n    in_brain = ~np.isin(beryl_all, NON_REGION_ACRONYMS)\n    keep = good & in_brain\n    keep_idx = np.nonzero(keep)[0]\n    return keep_idx, beryl_all[keep_idx], int(good.sum())\n\n\ndef load_trials(one, eid):\n    \"\"\"Trials table + reference trial mask (``load_trials_and_mask``).\"\"\"\n    from brainbox.io.one import SessionLoader\n    from utils.ibl_data_utils import load_trials_and_mask\n\n    sess_loader = SessionLoader(one=one, eid=eid)\n    trials, mask = load_trials_and_mask(one=one, eid=eid, max_trial_len=10.0,\n                                        sess_loader=sess_loader)\n    return sess_loader, trials, mask.to_numpy()\n\n\ndef load_continuous_behaviors(one, eid, sess_loader):\n    \"\"\"Wheel speed and whisker motion energy for the whole session.\n\n    Same sources as ``ibl_data_utils.load_target_behavior``:\n    wheel speed = |velocity| from ``SessionLoader.load_wheel`` (1 kHz,\n    Gaussian-smoothed), whisker motion energy from the left camera ROI motion\n    energy, falling back to the right camera when the left is unavailable.\n    \"\"\"\n    beh = {}\n\n    sess_loader.load_wheel()\n    beh['wheel-speed'] = {\n        'times': sess_loader.wheel['times'].to_numpy(),\n        'values': np.abs(sess_loader.wheel['velocity'].to_numpy()),\n        'source': 'wheel.velocity (abs)',\n    }\n\n    me = None\n    for view, cam in (('left', 'leftCamera'), ('right', 'rightCamera')):\n        try:\n            sess_loader.load_motion_energy(views=[view])\n            df = sess_loader.motion_energy[cam]\n            me = {\n                'times': df['times'].to_numpy(),\n                'values': df['whiskerMotionEnergy'].to_numpy(),\n                'source': f'{cam}.ROIMotionEnergy',\n            }\n            break\n        except Exception:\n            continue\n    if me is None:\n        raise RuntimeError('no whisker motion energy available (left or right camera)')\n    beh['whisker-motion-energy'] = me\n    return beh\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# binning / interpolation\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef bin_spikes(spike_times, spike_clusters, n_neurons, interval_begs, binsize=0.02,\n               n_bins=N_BINS):\n    \"\"\"Spike counts in non-overlapping bins for every interval.\n\n    Reproduces ``bincount2D(times, clusters, xbin=binsize, xlim=[t_beg, t_end])``\n    truncated to the first ``n_bins`` columns: bin ``k`` of a trial covers\n    ``[t_beg + k*binsize, t_beg + (k+1)*binsize)`` and only spikes with\n    ``t_beg <= t < t_end`` are counted.\n\n    `spike_times` must be sorted and `spike_clusters` must already be remapped\n    to 0..n_neurons-1.\n\n    Returns (n_intervals, n_neurons, n_bins) float32 array of counts.\n    \"\"\"\n    n_intervals = len(interval_begs)\n    out = np.zeros((n_intervals, n_neurons, n_bins), dtype=np.float32)\n    interval_ends = interval_begs + n_bins * binsize\n    i0s = np.searchsorted(spike_times, interval_begs, side='left')\n    i1s = np.searchsorted(spike_times, interval_ends, side='left')\n    for k in range(n_intervals):\n        i0, i1 = i0s[k], i1s[k]\n        if i1 <= i0:\n            continue\n        rel = spike_times[i0:i1] - interval_begs[k]\n        bin_idx = np.floor(rel / binsize).astype(np.int64)\n        np.clip(bin_idx, 0, n_bins - 1, out=bin_idx)\n        flat = spike_clusters[i0:i1].astype(np.int64) * n_bins + bin_idx\n        counts = np.bincount(flat, minlength=n_neurons * n_bins)\n        out[k] = counts.reshape(n_neurons, n_bins)\n    return out\n\n\ndef interpolate_behavior(times, values, interval_begs, binsize=0.02, n_bins=N_BINS):\n    \"\"\"Interpolate a continuous behaviour onto each trial's bin grid.\n\n    Follows ``ibl_data_utils.get_behavior_per_interval``: samples strictly\n    inside the interval are selected, then linearly interpolated (with\n    extrapolation) onto ``linspace(t_beg + binsize, t_end, n_bins)``, i.e. the\n    right edge of each spike bin.\n\n    Returns\n    -------\n    vals : (n_intervals, n_bins) float array (rows of NaN where invalid)\n    good : (n_intervals,) bool array\n    reasons : list of str or None, per interval\n    \"\"\"\n    interval_ends = interval_begs + n_bins * binsize\n    idxs_beg = np.searchsorted(times, interval_begs, side='right')\n    idxs_end = np.searchsorted(times, interval_ends, side='left')\n\n    n = len(interval_begs)\n    vals = np.full((n, n_bins), np.nan, dtype=np.float64)\n    good = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)\n    reasons = [None] * n\n\n    for k in range(n):\n        t = times[idxs_beg[k]:idxs_end[k]]\n        v = values[idxs_beg[k]:idxs_end[k]]\n        if len(v) == 0:\n            reasons[k] = 'target data not present'\n            continue\n        if np.isnan(interval_begs[k]) or np.isnan(interval_ends[k]):\n            reasons[k] = 'bad interval data'\n            continue\n        if np.abs(interval_begs[k] - t[0]) > binsize:\n            reasons[k] = 'target data starts too late'\n            continue\n        if np.abs(interval_ends[k] - t[-1]) > binsize:\n            reasons[k] = 'target data ends too early'\n            continue\n        if np.any(np.isnan(v)):\n            # the reference keeps these (allow_nans=True) and imputes the trial\n            # mean inside its data loader; a categorical target cannot be\n            # imputed without inventing a class, so the trial is dropped\n            reasons[k] = 'nans in target data'\n            continue\n        x = np.linspace(interval_begs[k] + binsize, interval_ends[k], n_bins)\n        vals[k] = interp1d(t, v, kind='linear', fill_value='extrapolate')(x)\n        good[k] = True\n    return vals, good, reasons\n\n\ndef discretize_tertiles(values):\n    \"\"\"Map a (n_trials, n_bins) continuous array onto {0, 1, 2} by tertile.\n\n    Thresholds are the 33.3 / 66.7 percentiles of all values pooled over the\n    session's retained trials, so each session's classes are balanced and the\n    arbitrary units of motion energy do not have to be comparable across\n    sessions.\n    \"\"\"\n    flat = values.reshape(-1)\n    q1, q2 = np.quantile(flat, TERTILES)\n    if not (q1 < q2):\n        # degenerate (heavily tied) distribution: fall back to the distinct\n        # quantile values that do exist so the labels stay monotone\n        edges = np.unique([q1, q2])\n        labels = np.digitize(values, edges, right=False)\n        return labels.astype(np.int64), (float(q1), float(q2))\n    labels = np.digitize(values, [q1, q2], right=False).astype(np.int64)\n    return labels, (float(q1), float(q2))\n\n\ndef trial_number_in_block(probability_left):\n    \"\"\"0-based index of each trial within its constant-``probabilityLeft`` block.\n\n    Computed on the *unfiltered* trials table, because the block structure is a\n    property of the experiment, not of which trials survive curation.\n    \"\"\"\n    p = np.asarray(probability_left, dtype=float)\n    # a change (including to/from NaN) starts a new block\n    changed = np.ones(len(p), dtype=bool)\n    if len(p) > 1:\n        same = (p[1:] == p[:-1]) | (np.isnan(p[1:]) & np.isnan(p[:-1]))\n        changed[1:] = ~same\n    block_id = np.cumsum(changed) - 1\n    # index within block = position - position of first trial of that block\n    first_of_block = np.zeros(block_id[-1] + 1, dtype=np.int64)\n    starts = np.nonzero(changed)[0]\n    first_of_block[:] = starts\n    return np.arange(len(p)) - first_of_block[block_id]\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# per-session conversion\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef process_session(task):\n    \"\"\"Convert one session. Returns a dict (or a dict with 'error').\"\"\"\n    eid, probe_rows, subject, lab, show_processing = task\n    t_start = time.time()\n    timings = {}\n    try:\n        warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')\n        one = get_one()\n\n        # ---- neural -------------------------------------------------------\n        t0 = time.time()\n        spikes, clusters = load_session_spikes(one, eid, probe_rows)\n        timings['load_spikes'] = time.time() - t0\n\n        keep_idx, beryl, n_good = select_neurons(clusters)\n        n_neurons = len(keep_idx)\n# Dataset Conversion Notes\n\n## Overview\n- **Dataset**: IBL Brain-Wide Map (BWM) public release — \"A brain-wide map of neural activity during complex behaviour\" (IBL et al.), ONE cache staged at `/app/data/one_cache`\n- **Method reference**: Zhang et al. 2026, *Neuron*, \"Exploiting correlations across trials and behavioral sessions to improve neural decoding\" (code in `/app/code/code_zhang2025`)\n- **Date started**: 2026-09-20\n- **Goal**: Convert to decoder-compatible format (`/app/converted_data.pkl`)\n\n---\n\n## Step 0: Setup and Initialization\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\nDirectory contents of `/app`:\n- `CONVERSION_NOTES.md` (this file)\n- `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yaml`, `stage_cache.sh`, `.manifest` — container plumbing\n- `datapaper.pdf` — IBL brain-wide map paper\n- `methodpaper.pdf` — Zhang et al. decoding paper\n- `dataarchitecture.pdf` — IBL data architecture white paper\n- `methods.txt` — excerpts of both papers\n- `code/` — `code_zhang2025/` (method reference code) and `ibllib/` (IBL library source)\n- `data/one_cache/` — ONE cache (release tables + symlinked lab/subject/session ALF trees)\n- `ibl_docs/` — downloaded ONE/ibllib/iblatlas documentation\n- `decoder.py`, `train_decoder.py` — decoder reference implementation and driver\n\nEnvironment verified:\n- `python3` works; \"Only sessions with at least 400 trials were retained\" |\n| Neural data time bin | **20 ms**, T = **100** | \"Recordings are split into 2-s trials, each divided into 20-ms bins, producing T = 100 time steps\" |\n| Behaviour sampling | 60 Hz (left cam) | \"wheel speed and whisker motion energy are time-varying signals sampled at 60 Hz\" |\n| Alignment for choice | stimulus onset, −0.5 → +1.5 s | \"For choice, we align trials to the stimulus onset, considering neural activity from 0.5 s before to 1.5 s post-onset\" |\n| Reward rate | ~0.85 (measured on example session) | task performance ≥90% on 100% contrast trials |\n| Block structure | first 90 trials at 0.5; then 0.2/0.8 blocks of 20–100 trials, mean 51 | \"After an initial 90 unbiased trials… empirical mean of 51 trials\" |\n| Contrast set | {0, 6.25, 12.5, 25, 100}% | data paper |\n| Choice decoding (Zhang, region `all`) | AUC 0.90 (all units) / 0.87 (good units) | example decoder outputs |\n| Prior decoding (Zhang, region `all`) | R² 0.27 / 0.18 | example decoder outputs |\n\n### Processing Details\n- **Alignment**: `stimOn_times`, window `(-0.5, +1.5) s` ⇒ 2 s interval.\n- **Binning**: 20 ms non-overlapping ⇒ T = 100. Spike bin `k` spans\n  `[stimOn − 0.5 + 0.02k, stimOn − 0.5 + 0.02(k+1))` (this is exactly what `bincount2D`\n  with `xlim=[t_beg,t_end]` does, and the reference then truncates to the first 100 columns).\n- **Continuous behaviour**: linearly interpolated onto `t_beg + 0.02·(k+1)`, i.e. the **right edge**\n  of each spike bin.\n- The method paper also describes 50-ms bins in a −0.5/+1.5 s window for choice and a\n  movement-aligned 0/+1 s window for the dynamic behaviours; the *released caching code*\n  (which is what is reproducible and which produces one dataset carrying all four behaviours)\n  uses the stimulus-onset 2 s / 20 ms / T=100 configuration, which is also the configuration\n  stated in the paper's Results (\"2-s trials… 20-ms bins… T = 100\"). The Decoder Task here\n  fixes stimulus-onset alignment, so that configuration is used.\n\n### Curation Steps\n\n**Neuron curation rules** (data paper \"Neurons and brain regions\"):\n- Exclude units failing any of the three RIGOR single-unit metrics: amplitude > 50 µV,\n  noise cut-off < 20 µV, refractory-period violation. Units passing all three are\n  \"well-isolated neurons\" (75,708 of 621,733). In the IBL cluster table this is exactly\n  `label >= 1` (`label` is the fraction of the three metrics passed: 0, 1/3, 2/3, 1).\n- Analyses further restricted to **grey-matter** regions in the Allen CCF, with ≥5 neurons\n  per session and recorded in ≥2 sessions.\n\n**Trial curation rules** (data paper \"Trials\", implemented in `load_trials_and_mask`):\n- Exclude a trial if any of `stimOn_times`, `choice`, `feedback_times`, `probabilityLeft`,\n  `firstMovement_times`, `feedbackType` is NaN.\n- Exclude if reaction time (`firstMovement_times − stimOn_times`) ∉ [0.08, 2.00] s.\n- Reference code adds `max_trial_len=10.0` (`feedback_times − goCue_times ≤ 10 s`) and\n  `exclude_nochoice=True` (`choice != 0`).\n\n### Decoders Trained (reference)\n| Decoded variable | Metric | Reference value (region `all`) |\n|------------------|--------|-------------------------------|\n| choice | AUC | 0.896 (all units) / 0.869 (good units) |\n| prior | R² | 0.270 / 0.182 |\n| wheel speed | R² | reported only in figures (single-trial R², ≈0.4–0.6) |\n| whisker motion energy | R² | reported only in figures (≈0.5–0.7) |\n\n---\n\n## Step 4: Check for Consistency\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Discrepancies Found\n| Topic | Code says | Data shows | Papers say | Resolution |\n|-------|-----------|------------|------------|------------|\n| Neuron quality filter | `load_spiking_data(qc=None)` ⇒ **all** Kilosort clusters | `label>=1` selects ~8–15% of clusters (76/898, 264/1728, 163/1202) | Method paper: \"bin spike counts using **all neurons**, sorted by Kilosort 2.5\"; data paper: analyses restricted to the **75,708 well-isolated neurons** | **Use well-isolated neurons (`label >= 1`)**. late'\n   286\t            continue\n   287\t        if np.abs(interval_ends[k] - t[-1]) > binsize:\n   288\t            reasons[k] = 'target data ends too early'\n   289\t            continue\n   290\t        if np.any(np.isnan(v)):\n   291\t            # the reference keeps these (allow_nans=True) and imputes the trial\n   292\t            # mean inside its data loader; a categorical target cannot be\n   293\t            # imputed without inventing a class, so the trial is dropped\n   294\t            reasons[k] = 'nans in target data'\n   295\t            continue\n   296\t        x = np.linspace(interval_begs[k] + binsize, interval_ends[k], n_bins)\n   297\t        vals[k] = interp1d(t, v, kind='linear', fill_value='extrapolate')(x)\n   298\t        good[k] = True\n   299\t    return vals, good, reasons\n   300\t\n   301\t\n   302\tdef discretize_tertiles(values):\n   303\t    \"\"\"Map a (n_trials, n_bins) continuous array onto {0, 1, 2} by tertile.\n   304\t\n   305\t    Thresholds are the 33.3 / 66.7 percentiles of all values pooled over the\n   306\t    session's retained trials, so each session's classes are balanced and the\n   307\t    arbitrary units of motion energy do not have to be comparable across\n   308\t    sessions.\n   309\t    \"\"\"\n   310\t    flat = values.reshape(-1)\n   311\t    q1, q2 = np.quantile(flat, TERTILES)\n   312\t    if not (q1 < q2):\n   313\t        # degenerate (heavily tied) distribution: fall back to the distinct\n   314\t        # quantile values that do exist so the labels stay monotone\n   315\t        edges = np.unique([q1, q2])\n   316\t        labels = np.digitize(values, edges, right=False)\n   317\t        return labels.astype(np.int64), (float(q1), float(q2))\n   318\t    labels = np.digitize(values, [q1, q2], right=False).astype(np.int64)\n   319\t    return labels, (float(q1), float(q2))\n   320\t\n   321\t\n   322\tdef trial_number_in_block(probability_left):\n   323\t    \"\"\"0-based index of each trial within its constant-``probabilityLeft`` block.\n   324\t\n   325\t    Computed on the *unfiltered* trials table, because the block structure is a\n   326\t    property of the experiment, not of which trials survive curation.\n   327\t    \"\"\"\n   328\t    p = np.asarray(probability_left, dtype=float)\n   329\t    # a change (including to/from NaN) starts a new block\n   330\t    changed = np.ones(len(p), dtype=bool)\n   331\t    if len(p) > 1:\n   332\t        same = (p[1:] == p[:-1]) | (np.isnan(p[1:]) & np.isnan(p[:-1]))\n   333\t        changed[1:] = ~same\n   334\t    block_id = np.cumsum(changed) - 1\n   335\t    # index within block = position - position of first trial of that block\n   336\t    first_of_block = np.zeros(block_id[-1] + 1, dtype=np.int64)\n   337\t    starts = np.nonzero(changed)[0]\n   338\t    first_of_block[:] = starts\n   339\t    return np.arange(len(p)) - first_of_block[block_id]\n   340\t\n   341\t\n   342\t# t0\n   417\t\n   418\t        # Drop trials in which not a single spike was recorded from the whole\n   419\t        # population over the 2 s window. With >= 5 simultaneously recorded\n   420\t        # neurons this indicates a dropout in the recording rather than a\n     1\t\"\"\"Convert the IBL brain-wide map into the decoder format.\n     2\t\n     3\tUsage: python -u convert_data.py <outpicklefile> [--full | --sample] [--datadir DIR]\n     4\t\"\"\"\n     5\t\n     6\timport argparse\n     7\timport datetime\n     8\timport os\n     9\timport pickle\n    10\timport time\n    11\timport warnings\n    12\tfrom concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, as_completed\n    13\t\n    14\timport numpy as np\n    15\timport pandas as pd\n    16\tfrom tqdm import tqdm\n    17\t\n    18\t_zhang2025_seed = 'x5cidj2hy87s'\n    19\tnp.random.seed(sum(ord(c) for c in _zhang2025_seed) % 2**31)\n    20\t\n    21\t# the loader always pulls these four spike arrays\n    22\timport brainbox.io.one as bio\n    23\tbio.SPIKES_ATTRIBUTES = ['clusters', 'times']\n    24\t\n    25\tfrom one.api import ONE, One\n    26\tfrom one.alf.exceptions import ALFWarning\n    27\tfrom brainbox.io.one import SessionLoader, SpikeSortingLoader\n    28\tfrom iblatlas.regions import BrainRegions\n    29\t\n    30\t# the trials table and the spike sorting are each listed at two revisions, and ONE warns\n    31\t# once per load that it is taking the later one, which is the one we want\n    32\twarnings.filterwarnings('ignore', category=ALFWarning)\n    33\t\n    34\t# --- constants ---\n    35\t\n    36\tHERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))\n    37\t# Directory holding the one_cache/ folder.  # is str, so a plain set intersection is empty whatever the contents. keep must\n   132\t    # stay UUID-valued for the `eid in keep` test below.\n   133\t    if subset_csv is not None:\n   134\t        subset_eids = set(pd.read_csv(subset_csv).eid.astype(str))\n   135\t        keep = {eid for eid in keep if str(eid) in subset_eids}\n   136\t        if not keep:\n   137\t            raise     return view\n   153\t    raise ValueError(f'no whisker motion energy for {eid}')\n   154\t\n   155\t\n   156\t# --- trials ---\n   157\t\n   158\tdef trial_variables(trials):\n   159\t    \"\"\"Choice, block prior and trial number in block, one row per trial.\"\"\"\n   160\t    # probabilityLeft is constant within a block, so a change of value starts a new block\n   161\t    block = (trials.probabilityLeft != trials.probabilityLeft.shift()).cumsum()\n   162\t\n   163\t    return pd.DataFrame({'choice': trials.choice.map(CHOICE),\n   164\t                         'prior': \"\"\"Trials whose window is spanned by this stream, allowing the one bin gap the reference allows.\"\"\"\n   170\t    start, stop = stim_on + T_START, stim_on + T_STOP\n   171\t    begin = np.searchsorted(times, start, side='right')      # first sample inside the window\n   172\t    end = np.searchsorted(times, stop, side='left') - 1       # last sample inside the window\n   173\t\n   174\t    # a trial with no sample at all, or a gap at either edge, has no usable trace\n   175\t    inside = begin <= end\n   176\t    first = np.where(inside, times[np.clip(begin, 0, times.size - 1)], np.inf)\n   177\t    last = np.where(inside, times[np.clip(end, 0, times.size - 1)], -np.inf)\n   178\t    return inside & (np.abs(start - first) <= BIN) & (np.abs(stop - last) <= BIN)\n   179\t\n   180\t\n   181\tdef usable_trials(trials, wheel_times, camera_times):\n   182\t    \"\"\"Trials the paper would keep, that also have a full wheel and camera window.\"\"\"\n   183\t    stim_on 194\t\n   195\tdef window_slice(times, stim_on):\n   196\t    \"\"\"Index range of each trial window, so a stream is sliced rather than rescanned per trial.\"\"\"\n   197\t    window_start = stim_on + window_start)\n   202\t    end = np.searchsorted(times, window_stop)\n   203\t\n   204\t    return begin, end\n   205\t\n   206\t\n   207\tdef trial_traces(times, values, stim_on):\n   208\t    \"\"\"A continuous trace resampled onto the same time grid for every trial.\"\"\"\n   209\t    begin, end = window_slice(times, stim_on)\n   210\t\n   211\t    traces = []\n   212\t    for trial, onset in enumerate(stim_on):\n   213\t        # one sample either side of the window, so the first and last bin centre are\n   214\t        # interpolated rather than clamped to the nearest sample inside it\n   215\t        first = max(begin[trial] - 1, 0)\n   216\t        last = end[trial] + 1\n   217\t\n   218\t        traces.append(np.interp(onset + TIME, times[first:last], values[first:last]))\n   219\t\n   220\t    return np.array(traces)\n   221\t\n   222\t\n   223\tdef discretize(trace):\n   224\t    \"\"\"Equal sized classes, split at percentiles of this session's regions.extend(brain_regions.acronym2acronym(clusters['acronym'][is_good], mapping='Beryl'))\n   262\t\n   263\t    times, units = np.concatenate(times), np.concatenate(units)\n   264\t\n   265\t    # np.array(regions)\n   268\t\n   269\t\n   270\tdef spike_counts(times, units, n_units, stim_on):\n   271\t    \"\"\"Spike count per unit and bin, for every trial.\"\"\"\n   272\t    counts = times[begin[trial]:end[trial]] - onset      # time from stimulus onset\n   277\t        spike_unit = units[begin[trial]:end[trial]]\n   278\t\n   279\t        bin_index = np.floor((spike_time - np.clip(bin_index, 0, N_BINS - 1)\n   283\t\n   284\t        # one flat index per spike lets a single bincount fill the whole unit by bin grid\n   285\t        flat_index = spike_unit * N_BINS + They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\\n  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\\n    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\\n    - audio: frequency, amplitude\\n    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\\n  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \\n  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\\n  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \\n\\n- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\\n  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal's output behavior or properties of the stimulus.\\n  - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. If a variable is not discrete, follow instructions from Decoder Task to discretize it. \\n  - Examples: stimulus properties (contrast, orientation), choice (left/right), reaction time, position\\n  - Can be time-varying or discrete values per trial. Negative means before event, positive after. \\n  - `off_end`: Signed time from alignment event to end of trial\\n  - Add other relevant fields, e.g. `session_info`\\n\\n## Python environment\\n\\n- All required Python packages are already installed in the system Python environment.\\n- Use `python3` to run any python code.\\n- If you need to install additional libraries, use `pip install`.\\n\\n## Decoder Reference\\n\\n- Run this script with `python /app/train_decoder.py <data_file_path>` to validate.\\n- Optional arguments:\\n  - `--verify-only`: Only verify data format and print summary, then exit (does not train decoder).\\n  - `--plot-samples`: Plot sample trials from data and save to png files.\\n  - `--cpu`: Force torch to use CPU only (use if GPU runs out of memory).\\n- Pipe the output to the designated file so that the user can examine it.\\n\\n### Purpose\\n\\nThese functions will be used during the validation phase to ensure:\\n1.
